# Kirby's Adventure: the whole ROM, documented from gameplay

The goal is every byte of *Kirby's Adventure* (NES, USA Rev A) — code, data, graphics, sound, the game's own
object-script language and its scripts — named, explained and backed by a check that a replay of real gameplay can
refute, with source generated from the documentation that reassembles to the original ROM byte for byte. The work is
done mostly by coding agents (Claude), under gates designed to catch them being wrong.

**Current progress: [`disasm/STATUS.md`](disasm/STATUS.md)**, generated by `kd status --md`. It is the only record of
progress; nothing here repeats its numbers.

## Method

**Evidence comes from running, not reading.** An instrumented build of the FCEUmm core
([`disasm/core/kd.patch`](disasm/core/kd.patch)) replays a corpus of verified input movies
([`disasm/corpus/`](disasm/corpus/)). Emulation is unchanged: every movie must end with the RAM hash the stock core
gives. The recording keeps, per PRG byte, whether it executed or was read, how often, by which instruction, and
first in which movie and frame. It also keeps every RAM/IO access pair, every control-flow edge, and which CHR tiles
the PPU fetched. On request it logs every instruction of a frame window, or of a routine's calls. Reading the code
forms a hypothesis; the recording decides.

**The documentation is a database; the source is generated.** `disasm/db/*.toml` has one unit per subsystem, keyed
by address: routines, data regions with their formats, RAM variables, script opcodes and scripts. The listing and the
ca65 source are rendered from ROM + evidence + database.

**Every description is paired with a claim the evidence can refute.** A name without a passing claim is only
*described*; the bytes of an entry that a passing claim is about are *verified*.

| claim | proves | checked on |
|---|---|---|
| `call` | what a routine computes, as an expression or a Python model over registers and memory in/out | every call in several windows of several movies |
| `frames` | an invariant that holds every frame and is not vacuous | frame windows |
| `effect` | causality: poke RAM, patch ROM or change input, compare against the untouched run | two runs from one savestate |
| `xref` | completeness: only these routines read / write / call it | every instruction the corpus ran |
| `static` / `format` | table contents; every byte of a format read by the instruction that reads that kind of byte | the ROM and the reader evidence |
| `vmlen` / `vmop` | a script opcode's layout and what its handler does | every execution |

**Gates, and a test of the gates.** `kd check` fails on any of these:
- an entry that contradicts the evidence (a name on an operand byte, a data region over executed code, overlaps);
- a failing claim;
- a generated source that does not reassemble to the ROM;
- a corpus movie that does not reproduce its RAM hash.

`kd selftest` plants a few hundred known errors (wrong models, omitted writers, misread formats, shifted tables, a
changed movie, a changed source line) and passes only when every one is caught. Its first run found two holes in the
gates themselves.

**Rounds.** One unit, one agent, one file. A subagent works from [`disasm/CARD.md`](disasm/CARD.md) on a scope from
`kd next` (the most-used undocumented chunks first), and is done when its unit passes with no weak claim. The
orchestrating session then merges the unit, adds the round's planted errors to the selftest and runs every gate.
[`disasm/PLAYBOOK.md`](disasm/PLAYBOOK.md) is the method in full.

**Coverage comes from gameplay first.** What no movie ran is not documented by reading it while gameplay can still
reach it. A routine nothing reached, or a branch that only ever went one way, becomes a driving task. An agent
writes the task as ordered conditions on named game state, plus conditions that must never hold. The `kt` driver
([`tas/DRIVER.md`](tas/DRIVER.md)) finds inputs with exploration search, and a replay from power-on in a fresh
process verifies the movie. The movie joins the corpus only if it adds code, data, edges or tiles. Bytes that no
reachable play runs are described from their bytes last, and stay marked as never run.

## Bring your own ROM

Nothing of the game is in this repository: no ROM, no extracted graphics or sound, no generated source. Everything
is produced locally from your dump of `Kirby's Adventure (USA) (Rev A)`, iNES file SHA-1
`f324e7c8c3ad102ecdcca011ecc494f6f345d768`, at `roms/usa-rev-a.nes`.

```sh
cd tas && uv venv --python 3.13 .venv && uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python numpy pillow && cd ..
nix build github:NixOS/nixpkgs/1c89083e451e891152365b799595cf7790a43325#libretro.fceumm --out-link tas/core-fceumm
disasm/core/build.sh   # instrumented core + cc65 from the same pinned nixpkgs (the RAM hashes depend on it)
cd disasm
./kd evidence          # replay the corpus on the instrumented core
./kd check             # every gate; renders out/src/*.s and rebuilds the ROM from it
./kd selftest          # the planted errors
./kd next              # what to document or cover next
./kd status --md       # rewrite STATUS.md
```

## Layout

| path | what |
|---|---|
| `disasm/db/` | the documentation (the units are listed in `STATUS.md`) |
| `disasm/corpus/` | the movies that count as evidence, with their RAM hashes |
| `disasm/*.py`, `disasm/kd` | recorder driver, ROM and script models, data formats, claim checker, renderer, CLI |
| `disasm/LEDGER.md` | the history of the rounds |
| `tas/drive.py`, `tas/kt`, `tas/xsearch.py`, `tas/nes.py` | the coverage driver: emulator workbench, exploration search, replay checks |
| everything else in `tas/` | history (below) |

## History

The project began as an experiment in autonomous play: an agent on the Claude API played the game to the ending,
compared controllers (search, a small decision model, cloned policies) and distilled a recipe for driving a game to
a described behaviour. That recipe is what now produces the coverage movies, and its first full playthrough is the
corpus movie `main`. The rest is kept as a record and is not maintained: the API harness, speedrun notes, tasks and
traces ([`tas/README.md`](tas/README.md), [`tas/RECIPE.md`](tas/RECIPE.md), [`tas/V2-LEDGER.md`](tas/V2-LEDGER.md)),
and a test of the recipe on a non-emulated, replay-only game (`tas/transfer/opensummoners/`). Footage and
measurements of that phase: **[The Trace Recipe](https://claude.ai/artifact/CxeyjUJkX3jKNw6Pmnmyir)**.

**[OpenRecet](https://github.com/Francesco149/openrecet)** carries the whole recipe to a game that is not emulated:
the Win32 engine of *Recettear*. It snapshots a full Win32 game process to get what an emulator gives for free.

`main` follows the route of TASVideos publication [3226M](https://tasvideos.org/3226M) through worlds 1-5, replaying
its first 78,090 input frames. The movie file itself is not redistributed
([`tas/knowledge/movies/`](tas/knowledge/movies/README.md)).
